scenario: H3 stop, edit and resume on the GPU through the app API: Save and stop partway, a new Job revision with another preview prompt, more steps and a doubled learning rate, then resume (#206)

hardware.gpu_power_note: The owner's fixed power limit (280 W of 350 W) and fan profile were left unchanged. Clocks varied with GPU temperature during the trial.

method.workspace: Isolated GPU acceptance workspace (.\acceptance.cmd's preparation with --mode gpu --settings <owner settings, read only> --prepare-only) under an ignored .cache trial folder. Only the configured model paths came from the owner's settings; output, cache and app state were new folders. The backend ran from this checkout (python -m musubi_gui --no-browser) with MUSUBI_GUI_STATE pointing at the workspace state, below-normal CPU priority.
method.dataset: The workspace's synthetic H3 acceptance dataset: one generated 124-frame 256x256 24 fps clip (a brightening blue field) with a same-stem 440 Hz WAV and a one-line caption. One clip at one repeat makes each epoch one step.
method.driver: A script sending the GUI's requests in order: PUT /api/jobs/{id}, POST /api/jobs/{id}/review, POST /api/runs/prepare {start: true}, polling GET /api/runs/{id} and /logs, POST /api/runs/{id}/control {save_and_stop}, GET /api/runs/{id}/states (Inspect saved states), PUT /api/jobs/{id} (the new revision), POST /api/jobs/{id}/review, POST /api/runs/{id}/resume-check, POST /api/runs/{id}/resume {job_revision}, then control {save} and {sample} on the segment.
method.vram_sampling: nvidia-smi whole-device memory.used every 2 s (includes about 870 MiB of desktop use); sampling can miss brief peaks.
method.step_time: The trainer's timing record (training seconds excluding previews, divided by step intervals) and per-step differences of upstream's progress-bar elapsed time, whole seconds.

control_fresh_run.purpose: A fresh Run of the second acceptance Job with the source's training settings, no previews and no saves, started right after the segment, to compare step time at the same GPU warmth. Stopped after 27 steps.

per_step_loss_avr_loss.note: Upstream's avr_loss; with one clip per epoch it is each step's own loss. Uniform timestep sampling makes it noisy step to step. Global steps; the segment's local steps are offset by 26.
per_step_loss_avr_loss.first_resumed_step: Step 27 resumed at 1.13; the fresh control Run, whose weights at step 26 are identical, had 1.14 at step 27. The restored RNG reproduced the continuing timestep and noise draw, and nothing restarted from step 1's 21.3.

lora_up_l2_norm.note: L2 norm over all lora_up tensors of each checkpoint; zero at initialisation, growing as training proceeds.
lora_up_l2_norm.reading: The resumed weights continue from the step-26 norm without a reset, and grow about 2.2 times faster per step after the learning rate doubled.

step_time_seconds.gpu_clock_note: Median power during busy training sampled 268 W in the source, 229 W in the segment and 240 W (1590 MHz SM, 70 C) in the fresh control right after it. The fresh, never-resumed control Run took as long per step as the resumed segment, so the slower later steps follow GPU temperature and clocks, not resuming.

limits: Synthetic one-clip data at 256x256 and rank 4 proves the mechanics of resuming, not useful learning or production-size capacity.
Upstream restarts its data order on resume; with one clip per epoch this trial cannot show data-position effects.
The first Save now coincided with the interval save at step 30; the later one at step 44 tests an off-interval save.
Whole-device VRAM sampled every 2 s includes desktop use and can miss brief peaks.
